My engineering work connects nanoscale manufacturing and materials integration with electrical measurement, multiphysics transport, and computational analysis.

## Nanofabrication and device integration

My research includes solid-state and hybrid nanopore fabrication, heterogeneous membrane preparation, electrical characterization, and integration into measurement systems. I applied and adapted the laboratory’s existing chemically tuned controlled dielectric breakdown (CT-CDB) method to multilayer structures combining silicon nitride with graphene, MoS₂, and hBN.

[Multilayer nanopore research](projects/heterostructures.qmd)

## Instrumentation and automation

I contributed to P.O.R.E. (Programmable Ohmic Research Engine), supporting electrical control, experimental instrumentation, fabrication workflows, platform characterization, and experimental validation.

My laboratory experience includes the Park Systems NX-12 AFM, JEOL SEM, Axopatch electrical measurement systems, and Sutter Instrument P-2000 laser micropipette puller, alongside equipment calibration, troubleshooting, and data acquisition.

[Programmable fabrication project](projects/instrumentation.qmd)

## Modeling and analysis

COMSOL finite-element simulations examine electric-field distributions and nanoscale transport. Signal processing, statistical analysis, event-feature extraction, and machine learning support comparisons across devices and experimental conditions.

[Computational methods](projects/modeling-ml.qmd)

## Undergraduate engineering research

### Aerodynamic performance of C-wing configurations

My undergraduate thesis used **ANSYS Fluent** to study Onera M6 wing configurations with forward and backward C-wing sweep. I compared these with a conventional wing, investigating drag and flow behavior under subsonic and supersonic conditions.

### Additive manufacturing in orthopedic surgery

I conducted a literature review of three-dimensional printing for surgical planning, patient-specific implants, and customized anatomical models. The review was published in [AIP Conference Proceedings (2023)](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0165255).

## Semiconductor coursework and laboratory exposure

Graduate coursework and laboratory exposure covered semiconductor fabrication fundamentals, cleanroom processing, photolithography, photoresist processing, mask alignment, thermal oxidation, diffusion, etching, metallization, and MOSFET fabrication and testing. This preparation complements my hands-on research in nanopore fabrication.
